page: Amazon Web Services r7g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores using the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 model running at 2.6 GHz. It offers 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The underlying hardware runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. No local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core performance and software compilation, alongside a top-tier Passmark memory score. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 6200.54 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 116.96 GB/sec. Multi-core stress-ng tests and Passmark database operations also rank in the top 25%. However, single-core performance is moderate, as shown by average scores in single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Additionally, LLM text generation for small models is relatively weak, though medium model text generation remains strong.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7g.16xlarge leverages the ARM-based Graviton architecture to deliver high resource density and strong memory throughput without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This instance is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale database operations, Redis caching layers, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
